description: The overall baseline price is the mean unit price over all individual products.

a.request: In `Products`, compute each `production_type_code`'s average `unit_price` (ignoring missing prices). Compute an overall baseline by averaging `unit_price` directly over all individual products (ignoring missing prices), so each product counts once and types with more products weigh more. Proceed only if the baseline exists. Keep the types whose average is above this baseline. Next, take the simple mean of the kept types' averages, and keep only the types whose average is also above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types: their type average price, how far their type average is above the overall baseline, and how far it is above the mean of the kept types.
a.sql:
WITH type_averages AS (
    SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS type_avg_price
    FROM Products
    GROUP BY production_type_code
),
baseline AS (
    SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS overall_avg_price
    FROM Products
),
above_baseline AS (
    SELECT t.production_type_code, t.type_avg_price, b.overall_avg_price
    FROM type_averages t
    CROSS JOIN baseline b
    WHERE b.overall_avg_price IS NOT NULL
      AND t.type_avg_price > b.overall_avg_price
),
kept_type_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(type_avg_price) AS mean_kept_type_avg
    FROM above_baseline
),
remaining_types AS (
    SELECT a.type_avg_price, a.overall_avg_price, m.mean_kept_type_avg
    FROM above_baseline a
    CROSS JOIN kept_type_mean m
    WHERE m.mean_kept_type_avg IS NOT NULL
      AND a.type_avg_price > m.mean_kept_type_avg
)
SELECT AVG(type_avg_price) AS avg_type_price,
       AVG(type_avg_price - overall_avg_price) AS avg_above_overall_baseline,
       AVG(type_avg_price - mean_kept_type_avg) AS avg_above_kept_type_mean
FROM remaining_types;

c.request: In `Products`, find each `production_type_code`'s average `unit_price` (ignoring missing prices) and keep the types whose average is above the overall average price, if that average exists. Next, take the simple mean of the kept types' averages, and keep only the types also above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types: their type average price, how far their type average is above the overall average price, and how far it is above the mean of the kept types. The overall baseline price is the mean unit price over all individual products.
c.sql:
WITH type_averages AS (
  SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS type_avg_price
  FROM Products
  WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY production_type_code
), overall_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS overall_avg_price
  FROM Products
  WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL
), above_overall AS (
  SELECT ta.production_type_code, ta.type_avg_price, oa.overall_avg_price
  FROM type_averages ta
  CROSS JOIN overall_average oa
  WHERE oa.overall_avg_price IS NOT NULL
    AND ta.type_avg_price > oa.overall_avg_price
), kept_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(type_avg_price) AS mean_kept_type_avg
  FROM above_overall
), remaining AS (
  SELECT ao.type_avg_price, ao.overall_avg_price, km.mean_kept_type_avg
  FROM above_overall ao
  CROSS JOIN kept_mean km
  WHERE km.mean_kept_type_avg IS NOT NULL
    AND ao.type_avg_price > km.mean_kept_type_avg
)
SELECT AVG(type_avg_price) AS average_type_price,
       AVG(type_avg_price - overall_avg_price) AS average_above_overall,
       AVG(type_avg_price - mean_kept_type_avg) AS average_above_kept_types_mean
FROM remaining;

b.request: Group products by `production_type_code`, calculate each type’s average `unit_price` using only non-null prices, and retain types whose average exceeds the mean `unit_price` across all products with non-null prices, provided that overall mean exists. Calculate the unweighted mean of those retained type averages, then retain only types whose average also exceeds that mean. Return one row with the unweighted mean of the remaining types’ average prices, the unweighted mean of their differences from the overall mean, and the unweighted mean of their differences from the first retained types’ mean
b.sql:
WITH type_averages AS (
  SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price
  FROM Products
  WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY production_type_code
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price
  FROM Products
  WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL
),
first_retained AS (
  SELECT ta.production_type_code, ta.avg_price, om.avg_price AS overall_avg
  FROM type_averages ta
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
  WHERE om.avg_price IS NOT NULL
    AND ta.avg_price > om.avg_price
),
first_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS avg_price
  FROM first_retained
),
remaining AS (
  SELECT fr.avg_price, fr.overall_avg, fm.avg_price AS first_mean_avg
  FROM first_retained fr
  CROSS JOIN first_mean fm
  WHERE fr.avg_price > fm.avg_price
)
SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS mean_average_price,
       AVG(avg_price - overall_avg) AS mean_difference_from_overall_mean,
       AVG(avg_price - first_mean_avg) AS mean_difference_from_first_retained_mean
FROM remaining;

d.request: In `Products`, calculate each `production_type_code`’s average `unit_price`, ignoring missing prices. Keep types whose average exceeds the overall mean unit price across all individual products, if that overall mean exists. Then calculate the simple mean of the kept types’ averages and retain only types whose averages exceed that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged across the remaining types: their average price, the amount by which it exceeds the overall mean price, and the amount by which it exceeds the mean of the initially kept types’ averages.
d.sql:
WITH type_averages AS (
    SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS average_price
    FROM Products
    WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY production_type_code
), overall_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS mean_price
    FROM Products
), initially_kept AS (
    SELECT ta.production_type_code, ta.average_price, om.mean_price
    FROM type_averages ta
    CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
    WHERE om.mean_price IS NOT NULL
      AND ta.average_price > om.mean_price
), initial_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_price) AS mean_initial_average
    FROM initially_kept
), remaining AS (
    SELECT ik.average_price, ik.mean_price, im.mean_initial_average
    FROM initially_kept ik
    CROSS JOIN initial_mean im
    WHERE im.mean_initial_average IS NOT NULL
      AND ik.average_price > im.mean_initial_average
)
SELECT AVG(average_price) AS average_price,
       AVG(average_price - mean_price) AS excess_overall_mean,
       AVG(average_price - mean_initial_average) AS excess_over_initial_kept_mean
FROM remaining;
